svg.title: Figure 1 · PX4 interface register
svg.desc: Every IF-PX4 interface with its ends, exchange and hazards
svg.text: The 9 IF-PX4 interfaces of the item definition: who sends what to whom, and which hazards each carries, and whether PX4Integration.sysml
models it as a connection. PX4 v1.16.2 is pinned; every interface is proposed.
flight state, position, status; freshness and source validity
posture, stationary flag for the launch/recovery envelope
recovery request, abort; contingency on lost link
charging handshake, rotor inhibit, energy isolation
Generated by tools/figures/integrations_readme.py from the item definition, PX4Integration.sysml, SSFs and SITL results. Proposed integration: not implemented, integrated or verified; SITL is
synthetic with no evidence credit. ↔ two-way, → one-way.

g.text: Terms: HAZ-nnn = hazard record (safety/hazards/HAZ-xxx-nnn.yaml) · IF-nnn = interface in the item definition (architecture/item-definition.yaml) · IF-PX4-nnn = PX4 integration interface
(integrations/px4/interface-contract.md) · PX4 = PX4 Autopilot, the open-source flight-control software candidate for SUS-A1 · SITL = software-in-the-loop simulation · SSF-nnn =
safety-significant software function record (safety/software/) · SUS-A1 = dockable observation UAV · SUS-A1-FC = PX4-based flight controller · SUS-A1-NAV = navigation sensors, camera and
telemetry · SUS-A1-PWR = UAV battery and power management · SUS-I1-INT = integration manager and PX4 command adapter · SUS-M1-CTL = mission, motion and balance control · SUS-M1-DCK = UAV
dock, retention, charging and release · SUS-M1-PIL = pilot station, restraints, displays and controls · SysML = Systems Modeling Language (SysML v2) · UAV = uncrewed aerial vehicle (drone)
